en: If no one comes on hearing your call, then walk alone.
Walk alone, walk alone, walk alone, walk alone.
If no one speaks a word, O you, O you, O unlucky one,
if all keep their faces turned away, if all are afraid—
you, speak out and say what is in your mind alone.
If all turn back, O you, O you, O unlucky one,
if, as you set out on the deep, wild road, no one looks back—
then the thorns of the road
you, under your blood-smeared feet, tread down alone.
If the light does not hold [?], O you, O you, O unlucky one,
if on a dark night of storm and rain they shut the doors of their houses—
then in the fire of the thunderbolt
set alight the ribs of your own breast and burn alone.
rom: yadi tora ḍāka śune keu nā āse tabe ekalā calo re.
ekalā calo ekalā calo ekalā calo ekalā calo re.
yadi keu kathā nā kaẏa, ore ore o abhāgā,
yadi sabāi thāke mukha phirāẏe sabāi kare bhaẏa—
o tui mukha phuṭe tora manera kathā ekalā balo re.
yadi sabāi phire yāẏa, ore ore o abhāgā,
yadi gahana pathe yābāra kāle keu phire nā cāẏa—
o tui raktamākhā caraṇatale ekalā dalo re.
yadi ālo nā dhare, ore ore o abhāgā,
yadi jhaṛa-bādale ām̐dhāra rāte duẏāra deẏa ghare—
āpana bukera pām̐jara jbāliẏe niẏe ekalā jbalo re.
notes: The romanization is a strict transliteration of the Bengali letters (the inherent vowel written as 'a'): 'ekalā calo' is sung ekla calo.
're' at the line ends is an intimate call to the person addressed, not translated.
line 2.4: 'mukha phuṭe', literally 'with the mouth opening', to speak out.
line 4.1: 'ālo nā dhare', literally 'does not hold the light': either no one holds up a lamp for you, or the lamp will not catch.
line 4.3: 'bajrānala', the fire of the thunderbolt (bajra, Sanskrit vajra).
